newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to remove public transport subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to remove public transport subsidies.

text.p: Venezuela will remove fuel subsidies paid to public transport and industry in two or three stages over the next year, Evanan Romero, Venezuela's deputy Minister of Energy and Mines, said on Monday.
Venezuelan public transport companies pay only a fraction of the true cost of fuel and the deputy minister said the huge subsidies were hindering greater use of gas.
"Public transport subsidies through gasoline prices will be reduced gradually in two or three stages so that people are encouraged to convert to natural gas," Romero told journalists on Monday.
These subsidies are different from those paid to private consumers and were introduced last year to protect the public from a 450 percent rise in prices to individual consumers.
Romero said the subsidies would be removed slowly to avoid a sudden inflationary impact.
